summary: Attacked the extraction of Betts–Stix, 'Galois sections and p-adic period mappings' (Ann. of Math. 201 (2025) 79–166; arXiv:2204.13674v1, the only arXiv version; the published text is not openly readable). The extraction has 100 items, 7 routes and 6 source issues, written by cc-442dc5 and accepted unchanged by REV-PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25 (cc-7b31c4). The recorded hash reproduces, and the whole paper was re-read in the TeX. Coverage is good: every numbered statement has an item, most statements are faithful, E1–E6 all hold, and the Dirichlet citation is right. Fourteen findings: one high, four medium, nine low. High: (2) item /24 widens Proposition 2.19 from Q_p^×- to Q̄_p^×-valued characters, and then it is false (a CM character of Q(i) at an inert p). Medium: (1) since make_queue's 28 September change, the paper is queued for design twice, as DESIGN-BETTS-STIX (#952, GaloisSectionsPadicPeriodMaps, which never points to the extraction) and as DESIGN-AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabautyPartII (#3475, whose only continuation is route 1). (3) Item /78 redefines Σ_A as Q̄_p-points, and E1's alternative repair 'A reduced (hence étale)' is false for the paper's Q_p-points (A = Q_{p²}); A must be split. (4) Shimizu's relative p-adic monodromy theorem [Shi20, Lemma 8.9] and his Proposition 4.9, on which Theorem 3.22 and so Theorem 3.3 rest, have no item, and P8 does not plan them. (5) Lemma A.2 is false under the reading its proof needs, and its use in Theorem 3.12(2) fits neither reading: a new gap. Low: (6) a new error, T for T⁻¹ in §5's period-map formula, copied into /67; (7) an explicit counterexample to Remark 6.23(I) (r_0 = 101, 2749 | q − 1, K = Q(√2749)), showing E6's reason is too narrow; (8) seven more unrecorded gaps and misprints (Remark 5.11 needs Y proper; Lemma 4.7 needs π proper; others); (9) /93 misstates Remark 6.23; (10) dropped hypotheses in /32, /44, /45, /68 and /79; (11) Mathlib's BDeRham and the Sp group schemes are not cited; (12) /11 cites DWP.4, which is projective-only; (13) /28 is not planned in LV.3 in this generality; (14) route 4 misreads footnote 1.

Source, fetched 30 September 2026. arXiv:2204.13674v1 PDF (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2204.13674v1, 59 pp.) has SHA-256 7d4b7d49c09b979ce4485251ea6f77527fcdb7c516ed7296d20c42e947ef0c18, matching the extraction. The arXiv e-print (https://arxiv.org/e-print/2204.13674v1) has SHA-256 0905aedc4ee02ea281f35c4497b5de8b70419fc808e50985e98b877472d87f11: main.tex with intro, reps, reps_in_families, abelian-by-finite, big_monodromy, locus, section_mordell and appx_derived; the bundled prelims.tex is not input by main.tex. The arXiv abstract page lists only v1 (28 April 2022). The Annals article page (https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2025/201-1/p02) gives the abstract only, with received 20 July 2022, revised 24 May 2024, accepted 28 May 2024, published online 9 January 2025. doi:10.4007/annals.2025.201.1.2 resolves to Project Euclid, which served an Incapsula bot block. Unpaywall lists no open copy. So the published text was not read, and every locator and finding here refers to arXiv v1.

Whole paper re-read in the TeX and checked against the PDF text layer (pdftotext), section by section: §1 (Definition 1.1, Theorems A and B, Remarks 1.3–1.6, Definition 1.7, Proposition 1.8, Remark 1.9, footnote 1); §2 (Definition 2.1 to Corollary 2.21); §3 (Definition 3.1 to Remark 3.29, including the proofs of Theorems 3.3, 3.12 and 3.22 and Proposition 3.20); §4 (Definition 4.1 to Lemma 4.12); §5 (Lemma 5.1 to Remark 5.11); §6 (Definition 6.1 to the proof of Theorem 6.5 in §6.5); §7 (Theorem 7.1, Proposition 7.2, (†)); Appendix A. Parallel sub-agents read the sections; every finding filed was re-checked personally at the quoted TeX line and PDF page.

Items. All 100 statements were compared with the source, and the locators with the PDF pages. Faithful, with every hypothesis: /1–/10, /12–/23, /26, /27, /29, /31, /33–/43, /46–/56, /58–/66, /69, /71–/76, /80–/92, /94–/98, /100, Theorems A and B (no CM subfield, genus ≥ 2, smooth projective, every finite v), and Theorem 6.5 (self-conjugate v, the Kodaira–Parshin family). Defective: /24 and /25 (finding 2); /77 and /78 (3); /99 (5); /67 (6); /57 and /70 (8); /93 (9); /32, /44, /45, /68 and /79 (10); /11 (12); /28 (13).

Recorded mistakes. E1 re-derived: the ε³ counterexample is valid under the paper's definition of a symplectic pair, which does not require A reduced, and it is S-good. The second repair is wrong (finding 3). E2 re-derived: the G_v-only step gives traces to K_{v,0}, and the Frobenius repair works. E3: (3.8), Proposition 3.19(2) and 3.20(7) are all for smooth proper varieties, so the total space of a line bundle is outside them. Both repairs, via O(D_1 − D_2) with cycle classes of possibly singular divisors computed through a resolution as in (7)'s proof, and via P(L ⊕ O), are valid. E4 and E5 were checked at locus.tex/abelian-by-finite.tex. E5 also occurs at l.343, p.49, which the locator covers. E6 is confirmed, with an explicit instance (finding 7). New mistakes are in findings 5, 6 and 8.

findings.claim: Item /24 states Proposition 2.19 for characters χ: G_K → Q̄_p^×. The paper states it for χ: G_K → Q_p^×, and with Q̄_p-values the statement is false. Counterexample: K = Q(i), p ≡ 3 mod 4, v = (p), which is inert and so self-conjugate by Definition 2.17, since its restriction to the CM field K is fixed by conjugation. Let E: y² = x³ − x, which has CM by Z[i] over K. G_K acts on V_pE, free of rank 1 over K ⊗ Q_p = Q_{p²}, through a character ρ: G_K → Q_{p²}^×. Take χ = ι∘ρ for an embedding ι: Q_{p²} → Q̄_p. χ is unramified outside {2, p}. It is pure of weight n = 1, since Frob_𝔮 acts by the Hecke character value ψ(𝔮), with |ψ(𝔮)| = N𝔮^{1/2} in every complex embedding. It is de Rham at v, since ρ|G_v is a Lubin–Tate character of Q_{p²}. So 'n is even and r_v = n/2' fails for a self-conjugate v. Moreover χ|G_v has Hodge–Tate weights 0 and 1 for the two embeddings, so 'the Hodge–Tate weight r_v' is not even well defined. Item /25 (Remark 2.20) is stated 'under Proposition 2.19's hypotheses' and inherits the error: here χ|G_v is Lubin–Tate, not χ_0·χ_cyc^{−n/2} with χ_0 of finite order. The proof uses Q_p-values essentially: η_p^alg is the product of N_{K_v|Q_p}^{r_v} with values in Q_p^×.
findings.evidence: arXiv v1 p.13, reps.tex l.329: 'Let χ: G_K → Q_p^× be a p-adic character such that: (i) χ is unramified and pure of weight n ∈ Z outside a finite set S …, and (ii) χ is de Rham at all p-adic places of K. … In particular, if v is self-conjugate, then n is even and r_v = n/2.' Also p.13: 'η_p^alg: (K⊗_Q Q_p)^× = ∏_{v|p} K_v^× → Q_p^× for the product of the maps N_{K_v|Q_p}^{r_v}'. Item /24 as written: 'Let χ: G_K → Q̄_p^× be unramified and pure of weight n outside a finite set and de Rham at all p-adic places, … for self-conjugate v, n is even and r_v = n/2.' Definition 2.17, p.13: 'a finite place is self-conjugate if it is conjugate to itself', where conjugate means that the restrictions to every CM subfield are complex-conjugate.
findings.fix: In item /24, replace Q̄_p^× by Q_p^× (the paper's hypothesis). In /25, keep 'Q_p-valued'. Route 1's design must plan the Q_p-valued statement.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25.result.json: item PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25/78 (and /77); sourceIssues PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25/E1 'correction'; report PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25.md, E1
findings.claim: The paper defines Σ_A as the Q_p-points of A, Hom_{Q_p-alg}(A, Q_p), with V_ψ = Q_p ⊗_{A,ψ} V. Item /78 silently changes this to 'Σ = Σ_A the Q̄_p-points of A', which is a different statement with Q̄_p-coefficient V_ψ that the paper does not prove. Item /77 likewise says 'Q̄_p-algebra maps'. E1's second repair, 'or assume A reduced (hence étale over Q_p), where #Σ_A = dim_{Q_p}(A)', is false for the paper's Σ_A: an étale Q_p-algebra need not be split. Counterexample: K = Q (every place self-conjugate), E/Q an elliptic curve, and A = Q_{p²} with trivial G_K-action. Take V = A ⊗_{Q_p} H¹_ét(E_Q̄, Q_p) (free of rank 2 over A, so d = 1), L = A(−1), and ω the A-linear extension of the Weil pairing. The pair is reduced, étale and S-good, but Σ_A = Hom(Q_{p²}, Q_p) = ∅. So (a) and (b) fail, and (c) as printed asks 0 ≥ dim(A)/(d+1) = 1. The first repair (#Σ_A in place of dim_{Q_p}(A)) is right. The alternative hypothesis must be 'A split', A ≅ Q_p^n as algebras, where #Σ_A = dim A. That is what every application has: A ≅ H⁰_ét(X_{y_v,K̄_v}, Q_p) = ∏ Q_p (Remark 6.6), and an S-good A with A|G_v ≅ H⁰ is then split. E1's ε³ counterexample itself, and its verdict, are right.
findings.evidence: arXiv v1 p.45, locus.tex l.108: 'Σ_A := Spec(A)(Q_p) = {ψ : A → Q_p ; Q_p-algebra homomorphism}'; l.126: 'V_ψ := Q_p ⊗_{A,ψ} V'. Proposition 1.8, p.5: 'Let Σ = Hom_{Alg(Q_p)}(A, Q_p) be the finite G_K-set of Q_p-algebra homomorphisms A → Q_p'. Proposition 6.7(c), p.46: 'the number of ψ ∈ Σ satisfying [G_v : G_{w_ψ}] < 4 is ≥ (1/(d+1)) dim_{Q_p}(A)'. Remark 6.6, p.46: 'H⁰_ét(X_{y_v,K̄_v},Q_p) = … = ∏_{ψ ∈ Y′_{y_v}(K̄_v)} Q_p'. The definition of a symplectic pair (abelian-by-finite.tex ll.70–95, pp.33–34) asks only for a finite-dimensional Q_p-algebra A with continuous action, V locally free over A and L free of rank 1. Item /78 reads: 'Σ = Σ_A the Q̄_p-points of A … (c) the number of ψ ∈ Σ with [G_v : G_{w_ψ}] < 4 is ≥ #Σ/(d + 1), which is ≥ dim_{Q_p}(A)/(d + 1) when A is étale.'
findings.fix: Item /78: restore 'Σ = Σ_A = Hom_{Q_p-alg}(A, Q_p), V_ψ = Q_p ⊗_{A,ψ} V', and replace the étale clause by 'which is ≥ dim_{Q_p}(A)/(d+1) when A is split (A ≅ Q_p^n)'. Item /77: 'Q_p-algebra maps'. E1 correction: 'Replace dim_{Q_p}(A) by #Σ_A in (c), or assume A split (A ≅ Q_p^n as a Q_p-algebra), where #Σ_A = dim_{Q_p}(A). Reduced or étale is not enough: A = Q_{p²} gives Σ_A = ∅.' Add the Q_{p²} example to E1's reason. Apply the same change to Definition 6.8(c) in item /79, which uses dim(A) in the same way.

findings.claim: The key external theorem behind the paper's model-free control of D_pst (Theorem 3.22, and so Theorem 3.3, Proposition 3.5 and everything in §§4–7) has no item: Shimizu's relative p-adic monodromy theorem [Shi20, Lemma 8.9, resting on his Theorem 9.7]. It says that a de Rham local system on a spherical polyannulus whose associated flat bundle has a full basis of horizontal sections is potentially horizontal semistable. Its companion [Shi20, Proposition 4.9], B_dR(R_v)^{G_{R_v}, ∇=0} = K_v, with the ring B_dR(R_v) := H⁰(Ū, OB_dR), is also missing. It is used to pin down the transport isomorphism up to GL_n(K_v). The extraction names Lemma 8.9 only in the prerequisites entry. Item /48 defines D^∇_pst and 'potentially horizontal semistable' but states no theorem that such local systems are potentially horizontal semistable. Without it, Theorem 3.22's proof has an unplanned step. The owner question is also open: route 6 sends Shimizu's period ring and specialisation lemmas (/48–/50) to P8, but P8's contract ('Shared relative period sheaves': A_inf, B_dR^+ and OB_dR sheaves, the Poincaré lemma, the proper-smooth comparison) does not plan a relative p-adic monodromy theorem. The absolute p-adic monodromy theorem is R06.3.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25.result.json: item PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25/99 (Lemma A.2), items /38 and /39 (Theorem 3.12, Lemma 3.14), sourceIssues
findings.claim: Lemma A.2 as printed is ambiguous, and in the reading its proof needs it is false. It assumes a filtration 'bounded below in every degree' and reduces to the degreewise bounded case. If 'bounded below' means F^pA^n = A^n for p ≪ 0, the reduction is invalid. Counterexample: A⁰ = A¹ = K with d = id, F^pA⁰ = K for p ≤ 0 and 0 for p ≥ 1, and F^pA¹ = K for all p. The only nonzero E₁ term is E₁^{0,0} = gr⁰A⁰ = K, so the spectral sequence degenerates at E₁. But H¹(F¹A) = K → H¹(F⁰A) = 0 is not injective, so H¹(A) is not filtered. If instead the hypothesis is F^pA^n = 0 for p ≫ 0, the lemma holds, but then the reduction step is superfluous. The one application fits neither reading. The proof of Theorem 3.12(2) applies Lemma A.2 to OB_dR,U ⊗_{O_U} Rπ_dR*E, whose filtration is nonzero in every degree and never equal to the whole module. That application also uses, with no citation and no item, that the relative Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence of a de Rham pair's pushforward degenerates at E₁. This is a gap in the proof of Theorem 3.12(2) (η^∧ is an isomorphism), which the paper presents as its own commentary on [Sch13, Theorem 8.8]. It is not recorded under sourceIssues, and item /99 reproduces the ambiguous hypothesis.
findings.evidence: arXiv v1 p.57, appx_derived.tex ll.25–29: 'Suppose that A is a filtered complex of sheaves of A-modules whose filtration is bounded below in every degree. If the spectral sequence associated to A degenerates at the first page, then H^j(A) is a filtered A-module for all j. Proof. It suffices to prove this under the additional assumption that the filtration is degreewise bounded above. In this case, A is a filtered complex with strict differentials by [Del71, Proposition 1.3.2] …'. p.22, reps_in_families.tex l.339: 'Both OB_dR,U ⊗_{Ẑ_p,U} Rπ_*𝔼 and OB_dR,U ⊗_{O_U} Rπ_dR*E have filtered cohomology objects …; the second of these follows from the fact that the relative Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence for E degenerates at the first page using Lemma A.2.' Remark 3.13, p.22: 'OB_dR,U is not complete for its filtration in general'. Item /99: 'If A is a filtered complex with filtration bounded below in each degree and its spectral sequence degenerates at the first page, then each H^j(A) is filtered [Del71, Prop. 1.3.2].'

findings.claim: A new mistake in the paper that the extraction copies. In the proof of Proposition 5.3 the period maps are written with the columns of T where the columns of T⁻¹ are meant. T solves dT = −ωT with T(0) = I, so it is the parallel transport T^∇_{y_0}: E_{y_0} → E_y, which sends a constant vector e to the horizontal section Te. The period map pulls F^iE_y = span(e_1,…,e_{m_i}) back along T(y), giving T(y)⁻¹(F^i), the span of the first m_i columns of T⁻¹. The span of T_1,…,T_{m_i} is instead the push-forward. For m = 2, T = [[1,0],[a,1]] and F¹ = ⟨e_1⟩, the paper gives the point (1 : a) and the correct point is (1 : −a). Nothing downstream changes: T⁻¹ satisfies d(T⁻¹) = T⁻¹ω with T⁻¹(0) = I, has coefficients in the same rings, and ι(T⁻¹) = ι(T)⁻¹, so Lemmas 5.5 and 5.6 and Proposition 5.3 hold with T⁻¹. There is a related misprint in the proof of Lemma 5.6: 'Z_∞ ⊆ P^N_{K_v}' should be P^N_C.
findings.evidence: arXiv v1 p.41, big_monodromy.tex: 'let Φ̂_{y_0} … classifying the filtration on K_v[[t]]^{⊕m} where F^i is the span of the vectors T_1,…,T_{m_i}' and 'the v-adic period map … is the map whose ith component is given by T_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ T_{m_i}'. p.40: 'a unique m × m matrix T … satisfying dT = −ω·T subject to T|_{t=0} = I_m'. p.39: the period map is 'the holomorphic map classifying the filtration … given by pulling back the filtration F^• along the parallel transport map T^∇_{ỹ_0}'. Item /28 (Definition 3.1): 'Φ_{y_0}(y) is the filtration on E_{y_0} pulled back from E_y by T^∇_{y_0,y}'. Item /67: 'both period maps are given by T_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ T_{m_i}'. The proof of Lemma 5.6 (p.42) reads 'The homogenous ideal of definition of Z_∞ ⊆ P^N_{K_v} is then the ideal generated by those homogenous elements F ∈ C[X_0,…,X_N]'.
findings.fix: Add sourceIssue PAPER-BETTS-STIX-25/E8 (kind error, affects nothing; locator: proof of Proposition 5.3, (5.1) ff., pp.40–42). Printed: 'F^i is the span of the vectors T_1,…,T_{m_i}'. Correction: 'the columns of T⁻¹', or equivalently the solution of dS = Sω, S(0) = I. Reason: the computation above. In item /67, replace 'T_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ T_{m_i}' by the wedge of the first m_i columns of T⁻¹.

findings.claim: E6 is right, but its reason understates the failure: 'K′ ∩ Q(ζ_{q−1}) can be Q(√±r) … if [K′ : Q] is even'. The intersection can be any subfield of Q(ζ_r), for a prime r | q − 1 with r ≥ r_0, whose degree divides [K′ : Q], including fields of odd degree. And the failure happens for the q the Remark actually chooses. Explicit instance: r_0 = 101. The least prime q with q ≡ 3 mod 4 and q ≡ 2 mod every odd prime below 101 is q = 3458351945918277637129653220997634107 (strong probable prime to bases 2–47). 2749 divides q − 1, and 2749 is a prime with 2749 ≡ 1 mod 4 and 2749 ≡ 1 mod 3. Take K = Q(√2749), which is real quadratic, or K the cyclic cubic subfield of Q(ζ_2749). Both are Galois (K′ = K), both contain no CM subfield, and r_0 = 101 exceeds every odd prime divisor of [K′ : Q]. Yet K ⊂ Q(ζ_2749) ⊂ Q(ζ_{q−1}), so 'K′ is linearly disjoint from Q(ζ_{q−1})' is false. The cubic case shows that an even degree is not needed.
findings.evidence: arXiv v1 p.54, locus.tex l.580: 'choose an auxiliary prime number r_0 ≥ 100 strictly greater than all odd prime divisors of [K′:Q], and let q be the least prime number congruent to 3 modulo 4 and congruent to 2 modulo all odd primes less than r_0. Then (3°) is automatically satisfied, K′ is linearly disjoint from Q(ζ_{q−1}) …'. The computation: the CRT class modulo 4·∏_{3≤ℓ<101} ℓ was searched upward for the first Miller–Rabin prime, which is q above, and (q − 1) mod 2749 = 0. E6 'reason': 'K′ ∩ Q(ζ_{q−1}) can be Q(√±r) for a prime r ≥ r_0 dividing q − 1, if [K′ : Q] is even and r ramifies in K′.'
findings.fix: Replace E6's reason with the general statement: K′ ∩ Q(ζ_{q−1}) = K′ ∩ Q(ζ_{(q−1)/2}) is ramified only at primes ≥ r_0 dividing q − 1, and can be nontrivial whenever such a prime ramifies in K′, whatever the parity of [K′ : Q]. Give the explicit instance r_0 = 101, q as above, K = Q(√2749) or the cubic subfield of Q(ζ_2749). E6's correction (take r_0 above every prime ramified in K′) is right and stays. 'affects: nothing' stands: for K = Q(√2749) the proportion bound in (I) still tends to 1.

findings.claim: Several further mistakes in the paper are not recorded. Gaps: (1) Remark 5.11 (p.43) concludes finiteness 'by compactness' of Y(K_v), but Corollary 5.10 and the Remark assume only 'a smooth curve'. Y(K_v) is compact only for Y proper. For Y = P¹ ∖ {0,1,∞} over Q_p with the Legendre family (full monodromy) and C = {p^{−n} : n ≥ 1}, every closed disc meets C in finitely many points, so the hypothesis holds, yet C is infinite. The paper applies it only to projective Y. Item /70 copies the missing hypothesis. (2) Lemma 4.7 (p.35) is stated for π smooth, but identifies H²_dR(X/Y)_y ≅ H²_dR(X_y/L), which needs π proper as well. For X = A² ∖ {0} → A¹, (x,y) ↦ x, the fibre H¹_dR jumps at 0. It is applied only to proper π. Item /57 copies 'smooth'. Misprints: (3) p.36: 'the Poincaré line bundle on X ×_{Y′} X' should be X ×_{Y′} X^∨ (as on pp.33–34). (4) (4.3), p.38: the product is indexed by y′_0 ∈ |Y′_{y_0}| but its factors are Res^{L_{w_i}}_{K_v} H_{y′_i}, the companion of E4. (5) p.29: 'Now we turn to the proof of Theorem 3.3' introduces the proof of Theorem 3.22 (the reduction to polyannuli). (6) p.50, proof of Lemma 6.17: 'Φ′_ij = (σ_j ⊗ φ^{m_j})(Φ′_i1) for all i' should be 'for all j'. (7) p.54, Remark 6.23(I): 'where r runs over odd prime factors of q' should be 'of q − 1'.
findings.evidence: arXiv v1 p.43, big_monodromy.tex: Corollary 5.10: 'Suppose that Y is a smooth curve over a finite extension K_v of Q_p …'; Remark: 'the whole set C must be finite by Corollary 5.10 and the fact that Y(K_v) is covered by a finite number of the neighbourhoods U_{y_0}(K_v) by compactness.' p.35, abelian-by-finite.tex l.177: 'Let π: X → Y be a smooth morphism of smooth varieties … (once we identify H²_dR(X/Y)_y ≅ H²_dR(X_y/L) in the usual way)'. p.36: 'where L = (1,λ)*P with P the Poincaré line bundle on X ×_{Y′} X'. p.38: 'H_{y_0} = ∏_{y′_0 ∈ |Y′_{y_0}|} Res^{L_{w_i}}_{K_v} H_{y′_i}'. p.29: 'Now we turn to the proof of Theorem 3.3, which we want to extract from [Shi20]. The first step is to reduce to the case of spherical polyannuli.' p.50: 'Φ′_ij = (σ_j ⊗ φ^{m_j})(Φ′_i1) for all i.' p.54: 'of places of K, where r runs over odd prime factors of q.'

findings.claim: Item /93 misstates Remark 6.23 twice. (a) Its condition '(2) q − 1 is prime to 4' can never hold for an odd prime q. The paper's condition is that q − 1 is not divisible by 4. (b) Part (III) says the least q for genus 3 is '11 for (1)–(3)', dropping the paper's qualifier 'with the modification of (3) for places of good reduction' (n_v replaced by 2). Without it, q = 11 fails (3) for n_v = 7: 7·ζ(6)·2³/10³ ≈ 0.0570 > 1/((5/2)·10 + 1) = 1/26 ≈ 0.0385. With n_v = 2 it holds (≈ 0.0163).

findings.claim: The report says that B_dR, Grassmannians and the rest were searched and that 'only Dirichlet's theorem applies directly', listing as near misses only IsLagrangian, the scheme pro-étale site and Module.Grassmannian. It misses two relevant pieces of the pinned libraries. (1) Mathlib has Fontaine's period rings BDeRhamPlus and BDeRham, in Scholze's generality for an integral perfectoid-type ring, together with WittVector.fontaineTheta. These are the rings in D_dR(V) = (B_dR ⊗ V)^{G_v} (items /14, /16) and the stalks of B⁺_dR,U (/33). Their Galois action and filtration are absent. (2) Mathlib has Matrix.symplecticGroup, and Tau Ceti has the symplectic group scheme Sp_{2m} as a closed subgroup scheme of GL_{2m} (TauCeti.Symplectic.groupScheme, with points identified with TauCeti.GLSymplecticFin). These are the groups in GSp-irreducibility (/12), the symplectic modules (/54) and full monodromy (/68). No status changes, since none of the items exists as stated, but the notes should cite these declarations so that the blueprint builds on them.

findings.claim: Item /11 states Example 2.2 for a smooth proper variety X. The layer it names, DWP.4, plans Weil I for smooth projective varieties only, and says that 'general smooth proper nonprojective varieties belong to the later DWP.7 consequence'. The paper has the same imprecision: it cites [Del74, Théorème 1.6], which is Weil I's theorem for projective smooth varieties, for purity and integrality of smooth proper ones. Every use in the paper is to H¹ of abelian varieties, which are projective, so nothing is affected.

findings.claim: Item /28 is marked planned in LV.3, but LV.3 does not plan it in the paper's generality. Definition 3.1 defines the v-adic period map for any filtered vector bundle with flat connection on Y^an, on a rigid neighbourhood of any K_v-point, for any finite K_v/Q_p, landing in the flag variety of all filtrations. LV.3 plans Φ_v only on residue disks Ω_v(y_0) of a good model, with K_v/Q_p unramified and p > 2, through the formal horizontal sections of LV.2. The extraction itself marks the construction Definition 3.1 is built from, parallel transport on rigid neighbourhoods (/27), as missing and routes it to LV.3. The status of /28 is therefore inconsistent: it is missing in this generality.

findings.claim: Route 4's reason says: 'As the paper's footnote 1 notes, the K_v-centred version is needed even for [LV20]'s own argument.' Footnote 1 says something narrower. LV's argument does not quite prove the obstruction reformulation (2°), finiteness of the whole locus Y(K_v)^LV_{X_q,S}, because LV §3.4 treats only discs centred on K-points. LV's own proof of Mordell needs only K-centred discs. Relatedly, the route calls §5's lemmas redone 'without a model'. The model-free part is §3 (Theorem 3.22); §5's novelty is centring at K_v-points and comparing through ι: K_v ↪ C.
